issues.body: parse_request uses obj.get("source").and_then(|s| s.as_str()), so a present malformed value such as {"source":null,"dataset":"..."} or {"source":false,"dataset":"..."} becomes None and defaults to AuthzSource::Body. This selector chooses whether authorization trusts the server's loaded store or a caller-supplied dataset, so malformed input must not silently cross into the body lane. The stated fail-closed contract and unknown-source rejection currently cover only unknown strings, leaving this type-confusion path untested.
issues.fix_hint: Distinguish an absent key from a present value: match obj.get("source") directly, default only on None, accept only Value::String containing body/server, and return 400 for every other JSON type. Add a wire-level or parse_request test for at least source:null (with an otherwise valid dataset) asserting BAD_REQUEST.
issues.title: Non-string source values silently select the body authorization lane

verdict.summary: The generation-keyed stateful authorization view and its ACL-write integration test are coherent, but the new source selector is not fully fail-closed. A present JSON value of the wrong type is collapsed into the historical absent/default case, which can select the caller-supplied body dataset across a trust-boundary mistake. Reject every present value other than a string equal to body or server.
